results.title: Symmetry criterion for matrices indexed by a product
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A matrix on a product is symmetric exactly when its restrictions to each row and column are symmetric and both diagonals of every ordered rectangle agree in opposite directions.

results.title: Symplectic matrices have determinant one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $l$ a finite set, $I$ the identity matrix indexed by $l$, and $J = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & -I \\ I & 0 \end{pmatrix}$ the matrix over $R$ indexed by the disjoint union $l \sqcup l$. Every square matrix $A$ over $R$ indexed by $l \sqcup l$ with $A J A^{\mathsf{T}} = J$ satisfies $\det A = 1$.

results.title: Beatty term
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a positive integer $n$ and a real number $\alpha$, the Beatty term $b_n(\alpha)$ is the natural number $\max(\lfloor n/\alpha \rfloor, 0)$: the $n$-th term $\lfloor n \cdot (1/\alpha) \rfloor$ of the Beatty sequence of slope $1/\alpha$, truncated at $0$. Division by zero is read as $0$, so $b_n(0) = 0$.

results.title: Beatty term as a natural-number floor
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every positive integer $n$ and every real number $\alpha$, the Beatty term $b_n(\alpha)$ equals the natural-number floor of $n/\alpha$: the largest natural number $m$ with $m \le n/\alpha$ when $n/\alpha \ge 0$, and $0$ when $n/\alpha < 0$. Division by zero is read as $0$, so $n/0 = 0$.

results.title: Three-way partition of the positive integers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Three sequences $s_1, s_2, s_3$ of natural numbers indexed by the positive integers partition the positive integers when their ranges are pairwise disjoint, that is, $s_i(m) \ne s_j(n)$ for all $i \ne j$ and all positive integers $m$ and $n$, and the union of their ranges is exactly the set of positive integers: a natural number $k$ is a value of some $s_i$ if and only if $k > 0$.

results.title: Almost Beatty partition

results.title: Beatty's theorem and its converse
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be positive real numbers. The set of the numbers $\lfloor k\alpha\rfloor$ for positive integers $k$ and the set of the numbers $\lfloor k\beta\rfloor$ for positive integers $k$ are disjoint and their union is the set of positive integers if and only if $\alpha$ is irrational and $\alpha^{-1} + \beta^{-1} = 1$.

results.title: Counting $\beta$-Beatty terms between $\lfloor n\alpha\rfloor$ and $\lfloor n\beta\rfloor$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be an irrational number with $1 < \alpha < 2$, let $\beta$ be a real number with $\alpha^{-1} + \beta^{-1} = 1$, and let $B$ be the set of the numbers $\lfloor k\beta\rfloor$ for positive integers $k$. Then for every positive integer $n$, the number of elements of $B$ in the open interval $(\lfloor n\alpha\rfloor, \lfloor n\beta\rfloor)$ equals $\lfloor n(2 - \alpha)\rfloor$.

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a real number $x$, this is $|x - r|$, where $r$ is the integer nearest to $x$ (halves rounded up); equivalently, it is the minimum of $|x - n|$ over all integers $n$.

results.title: Einsiedler–Katok–Lindenstrauss theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a real number $x$, write $\lVert x \rVert$ for the distance from $x$ to the nearest integer. The set of pairs $(\alpha, \beta)$ of real numbers with $\liminf_{n \to \infty} n \cdot \lVert n\alpha \rVert \cdot \lVert n\beta \rVert > 0$, the lower limit taken over natural numbers $n$, has Hausdorff dimension $0$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$.

results.title: Corridor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The corridor is the L-shaped set of points $z \in \mathbb{C}$ with $\operatorname{Re} z \le 1$ and $0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 1$ (the horizontal arm, extending to the left) together with the points $z$ with $0 \le \operatorname{Re} z \le 1$ and $\operatorname{Im} z \ge 0$ (the vertical arm, extending upward): two perpendicular semi-infinite arms of width one.

results.title: Entrance of the corridor
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The entrance region of the unit right-angle corridor is the closed half-strip $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : \operatorname{Re} z \le 0,\ 0 \le \operatorname{Im} z \le 1\}$, the part of its horizontal arm to the left of the corner square.

results.title: Exit of the corridor
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Planar rigid motion

results.title: Position under a rigid motion

results.caption: Definition

results.title: Arc sets
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, an arc set on $n$ points is a finite set of ordered pairs $(i, j)$, called arcs, with $i, j \in \{0, 1, \dots, n - 1\}$.

results.title: Noncrossing arc sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An arc set $P$ on $n$ points is noncrossing when every arc $(i, j) \in P$ has $i < j$ and any two distinct arcs $(i, j)$ and $(k, l)$ of $P$ satisfy $i \ne k$, $j \ne l$, and not $i < k < j < l$. So distinct arcs do not cross and share neither a left nor a right endpoint.

results.title: Toggle at an arc
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an arc $a = (i, j)$ and an arc set $P$ on $n$ points, the toggle $\tau_{i,j}$ sends $P$ to $P \setminus \{a\}$ if $a \in P$; otherwise to $P \cup \{a\}$ if $P \cup \{a\}$ is a noncrossing arc set; and otherwise it leaves $P$ unchanged.

results.title: Toggle order
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the toggle order on $n$ points is the list of all arcs $(i, i + d)$ with $d \ge 1$, $i \ge 0$ and $i + d \le n - 1$, ordered by length $d = 1, \dots, n - 1$ and, for each length, by increasing left endpoint $i$. In $1$-indexed form it is $(1,2), (2,3), \dots, (n-1,n), (1,3), \dots, (n-2,n), \dots, (1,n)$.

results.title: Toggle composite
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The toggle composite $\sigma$ on $n$ points sends an arc set $P$ on $n$ points to the arc set obtained from $P$ by applying the toggles $\tau_{i,j}$ at the arcs $(i, j)$ of the toggle order on $n$ points one after another, in the order of that list.

results.title: Block count

results.title: Block-count homomesy claim for toggling noncrossing partitions
